note: Hover tooltips for section titles. 'concepts' paraphrase the book's definitions (page cited); each section's 'does' describes what the prototype screen does and is not book text.

trait.name: Trait
trait.text: An enduring part of your character's nature. Every character has at least one trait: their species.

attribute.name: Attributes
attribute.text: Six ratings (Control, Daring, Fitness, Insight, Presence, Reason) for your physical and mental capabilities and the way you approach problems. For humanoids they range from 7 to 12; 8 is average.

discipline.name: Departments
discipline.text: Six areas of expertise (Command, Conn, Engineering, Security, Science, Medicine), matching a starship's departments. Each is rated from 0 to 5.

focus.name: Focus
focus.text: A short description of a narrower skill, topic, or activity. Focuses improve your odds at tasks they apply to and can be used with any department.

value.name: Value
value.text: A short statement of a core belief or conviction. Values define who your character is and can give them an extra push to succeed in difficult situations.

talent.name: Talent
talent.text: An additional benefit that defines an area of specialty or a personal approach, such as extra d20s, re-rolls, bonus Momentum, or using a different department in a situation. Many talents have requirements that must be met before they can be chosen. A finished character has four talents; they are separate from the Species Ability, Species Trait, Focuses and Values.

assignment.name: Assignment
assignment.text: Your job aboard ship. Core lists the senior staff roles main characters may fill; in this prototype each assignment gives the role of the same name.

role.name: Role
role.text: Your character's place within the crew, from Star Trek Adventures 2E. Each role defines the character's job and comes with a distinct in-game benefit, the Role Benefit. Role Benefits work like talents but come from your role and cannot be chosen as talents.

rank.name: Rank
rank.text: Your place in the chain of command. Starfleet officers run from Cadet to Fleet Admiral; enlisted personnel run from Crewman to Master Chief Petty Officer. Your Experience may limit which ranks you can choose, and civilians do not need a rank.

speciesScreen.title: Species
speciesScreen.what: Book Step One. Your species is your character's first trait and raises three attributes by 1.
speciesScreen.does: Choose a species card and a gender, then complete any trait details and attribute choices below. The species' Species Ability (from Star Trek Adventures 2E) is shown under its name.

speciesGender.title: Gender
speciesGender.what: Decides which portraits you can pick on Finishing Touches.
speciesGender.does: Choose Male, Female, or Other. Other can use any portrait for the species. Gender has no effect on attributes, departments, values, focuses, traits, or any rule, and it is separate from pronouns.

environmentScreen.title: Environment
environmentScreen.what: Book Step Two. The kind of place where your character was raised. It grants one value, +1 to one attribute, and +1 to one department.
environmentScreen.does: Pick an environment card, then choose the value, attribute, and department below.

earlyOutlookScreen.title: Upbringing
earlyOutlookScreen.what: Book Step Three. The culture your character grew up in and whether they accepted or rebelled against it. It grants three attribute points across two attributes, +1 to one department, one focus, and one talent.
earlyOutlookScreen.does: Choose an Upbringing card, then accepted or rebelled, one department, one focus, and one talent.

educationScreen.title: Career Path
educationScreen.what: Book Step Four: Career Path. Your higher education and current profession. Each Career Path grants a trait, one value, three attribute points, department increases, three focuses, and one talent.
educationScreen.does: Choose a Career Path card and one of its options, then its trait (where Core offers two names) and the choices in the numbered sections, ending with one talent.

careerScreen.title: Career
careerScreen.what: Book Step Five: Experience (Novice, Experienced or Veteran) grants one value and one talent. Your assignment sets your department and role (Core pp.135–139), and your rank comes from Core p.140.
careerScreen.does: Choose your Experience and its value, then your assignment and rank. Your Experience also sets your talent: Novice receives Untapped Potential, Veteran receives Veteran, and Experienced chooses one.

careerHistoryScreen.title: Career History
careerHistoryScreen.what: Book Step Six. Two defining events in your career. Each raises one attribute and one department by 1 and grants one focus.
careerHistoryScreen.does: Choose two different events, then complete each one's attribute, department, and focus.

finishingTouchesScreen.title: Finishing Touches
finishingTouchesScreen.what: Book Step Seven. One final value; any attribute or department over the limits is brought back within them, then +1 to two attributes and two departments (still within the limits); personal details such as name and age, and an optional pastime.
finishingTouchesScreen.does: Work through each card: final value, attributes, departments, your fourth talent, portrait, name, pronouns and age, an optional pastime, and optional notes.

reviewScreen.title: Character Complete
reviewScreen.does: Check each section, fix anything under Needs Attention, then Confirm Character. Export JSON (Dev) downloads the character as a .json file.

reviewStatus.title: Status
reviewStatus.what: Checks your character against the finished-character requirements: every step complete, a name and pronouns, attributes total 56, departments total 16, four values, six focuses, four legal talents, and no duplicate values, focuses or talents.
reviewStatus.does: Lists each problem with a link to the screen that fixes it. When nothing is listed, Confirm Character becomes available.

reviewIdentity.title: Identity
reviewIdentity.what: Who your character is: name, gender, pronouns, species, species trait, and portrait. Gender is a presentation detail only.
reviewIdentity.does: Summary only. Change these on Species and Finishing Touches.

reviewOrigin.title: Origin & Early Life
reviewOrigin.what: Where your character was raised and the culture they grew up in.
reviewOrigin.does: Summary only. Change these on Environment and Upbringing.

reviewAttributes.does: Your final scores. The book's finished character has an attribute total of 56, no attribute above 12, and only one at 12. Change them on Finishing Touches.

reviewDisciplines.does: Your final scores. The book's finished character has a department total of 16, no department above 5, and only one at 5. Change them on Finishing Touches.

reviewEducation.title: Career Path
reviewEducation.what: Your character's Career Path option, its category, and the trait it grants.
reviewEducation.does: Summary only. Change it on Career Path.

reviewCareer.title: Career
reviewCareer.what: Your Experience, assignment, department, rank, and role.
reviewCareer.does: Summary only. Change these on Career. Posting will be chosen with your ship, which is not built yet.

reviewEvents.title: Career Events
reviewEvents.what: The defining events of your career and what each one gave you.
reviewEvents.does: Summary only. Change them on Career History.

reviewValues.does: Every value and the screen it came from. The book's finished character has four values.

reviewFocuses.does: Every focus and the screen it came from. The book's finished character has six focuses.

reviewTalents.does: Your four Character Talents and the screen that granted each. The Species Ability is listed under Identity, not here. Change a talent on the screen it came from.

reviewRoleBenefit.does: The benefit your role gives you. It is not one of your four talents and not your Species Ability. Your role comes from your assignment on Career.

reviewTraits.does: Your traits and their descriptions. Your species trait changes on Species; your Career Path trait changes with your Career Path.

reviewEquipment.title: Equipment
reviewEquipment.what: Standard-issue gear, assigned automatically from your department, assignment and rank, plus the background notes you wrote on Finishing Touches. Sidearm (Core p.141): Starfleet personnel receive a phaser type-1; security personnel and officers of lieutenant commander or higher receive a phaser type-2 instead; civilians receive none.
reviewEquipment.does: Summary only. Equipment changes with your assignment, department and rank on Career. Notes are free text the rules never read.

speciesTraits.does: Your species becomes your first trait automatically. Mixed Heritage and New Species ask for extra details here.

speciesAttributes.does: Shows the three attributes your species raises by +1. Some species let you choose which three.

environmentValue.does: Choose one value that reflects the environment and culture you were raised in: an example value of your species (or, for Another Species' World, of the species you were raised among), one of the book's sample values, or your own.

environmentAttribute.does: Raise one attribute by +1. The attributes offered depend on the environment you chose.

environmentDiscipline.does: Raise one department by +1, from those your environment offers.

outlookAttribute.does: Choose whether you accepted or rebelled against your Upbringing; each gives its own attribute bonuses.

outlookDiscipline.does: Raise one department by +1, from those your Upbringing offers.

outlookFocus.does: Choose one focus relating to your Upbringing: a book example, one of the book's sample focuses, or your own.

educationOptions.title: Career Path Options
educationOptions.what: Your higher education and current profession. Each option grants a trait, a value, attribute points, departments, and focuses.
educationOptions.does: Pick one option from the Career Path chosen above. The numbered sections below then apply its benefits.

educationDetails.title: Career Path Details
educationDetails.what: The book's description and rules for the option you selected, and the trait it grants.
educationDetails.does: Where Core names two traits (Diplomat or Ambassador, Scientist or Engineer), pick one here. Otherwise reference only.

educationAttributes.does: Spend the attribute points your Career Path gives. The instruction shows how many points and any limits.

educationDisciplines.does: Choose the departments your Career Path improves. Some options also allow an optional department swap.

educationFocuses.does: Choose the focuses your Career Path gives: book examples, the Focus Matrix, or your own.

educationValue.does: Choose one value you gained from your Career Path: one of Core's examples for your path (listed first), a sample value, or your own.

careerValue.does: Choose one value that fits your Experience: a Core example for Novice or Veteran (listed first), a sample value, or your own. Core says a Novice's value must reflect inexperience and a Veteran's their years of experience; an Experienced character's is chosen freely.

careerAssignment.does: Choose your job aboard ship. It sets your department and your role (with its Role Benefit). Only Commanding Officer has a minimum rank (Commander), so it is closed to Novice and enlisted characters.

assignmentDetails.title: Assignment Details
assignmentDetails.what: The department, any minimum rank, and description for your assignment, plus the role it gives you and that role's benefit (Core pp.135–139).
assignmentDetails.does: Reference only, except when the book names no department; then choose one here.

careerRank.does: Choose your rank. Your Career Path decides the ladder: Starfleet (Officer) and Starfleet (Intelligence) use officer ranks, Starfleet (Enlisted) uses enlisted ranks, and diplomats and civilians hold No Rank by default but may take an officer rank. A Commanding Officer must be at least Commander; a Novice can rank no higher than Lieutenant (junior grade) or Petty Officer, and a Veteran no lower than Lieutenant Commander or Chief Petty Officer. Your rank and department also decide your sidearm (Core p.141).

eventAttribute.does: Raise one attribute by +1. Most events set it; some let you choose.

eventDiscipline.does: Raise one department by +1. Most events set it; some let you choose.

eventFocus.does: Choose one focus reflecting this event: a book suggestion, one of the book's sample focuses, or your own.

eventDetails.title: Event Details
eventDetails.what: The book's description and effects for the selected event.
eventDetails.does: Reference only; nothing to choose here.

finalValue.does: Choose your last value. It might reflect your career events, another part of your character, or a relationship with someone in the crew or another culture.

talent.does: Choose this step's talent. Talents you don't qualify for, or already hold, are greyed out with the reason; switch the list to see them. Some talents also ask for a department, attribute, focus or attack type. Hover a talent for its full text.

talentDetails.title: Talent Details
talentDetails.what: The talent chosen here, with its requirements and book text, and every talent you have chosen so far.
talentDetails.does: Reference only, apart from any choice the talent needs.

valueDetails.title: Value Details
valueDetails.what: The book's text for this step and every value you have chosen so far.
valueDetails.does: Reference only; nothing to choose here.

attributeIncreases.does: After any scores over the limits have been brought down, add +1 to two different attributes. Each row shows the score after the limits and the final score; a +1 that would break the limits is unavailable.

attributeDetails.title: Attribute Details
attributeDetails.what: The book's text for this step and the attribute limits.
attributeDetails.does: If a lifepath score is over the limit, it is reduced first; choose where each reduced point goes here. The total must come out exactly right.

disciplineIncreases.does: After any departments over the limits have been brought down, add +1 to two different departments. Each row shows the score after the limits and the final score; a +1 that would break the limits is unavailable.

disciplineDetails.title: Department Details
disciplineDetails.what: The book's text for this step and the department limits.
disciplineDetails.does: If a lifepath score is over the limit, it is reduced first; choose where each reduced point goes here. The total must come out exactly right.

characterName.title: Name
characterName.what: Your character's name. Type one or roll a random male, female, or mixed name.
characterName.does: Required. Becomes the exported file's name. The same name is edited on the Name & Pronouns card.

nameAndPronouns.title: Name & Pronouns
nameAndPronouns.what: Your character's name, pronouns, and age.
nameAndPronouns.does: Name and pronouns are required; age is optional. The name becomes the exported file's name. Pick a pronoun set or type your own.

identityDetails.title: Identity Details
identityDetails.what: The book's guidance on pronouns and on age for your Experience.
identityDetails.does: Reference only; nothing to choose here.

pastime.title: Pastime
pastime.what: A hobby or passion your character enjoys off duty, or an interest unrelated to their duties.
pastime.does: Optional. Type your own or start from one of the book's categories. Saved and exported with your character; it has no rule effect in this prototype.

pastimeDetails.title: Pastime Details
pastimeDetails.what: The book's text on pastimes and its suggestion categories.
pastimeDetails.does: Reference only; nothing to choose here.

portraitOptions.title: Portrait
portraitOptions.what: How your character looks on the character sheet.
portraitOptions.does: Choose a preset portrait. The presets shown match the species and gender chosen on Species. Portraits are presentation only and have no game-rule effect.

portraitDetails.title: Portrait Details
portraitDetails.what: Controls for browsing the portrait presets.
portraitDetails.does: Step through the presets one at a time.

backgroundNotes.title: Background Notes
backgroundNotes.what: Optional free text about your character's history, personality, and relationships.
backgroundNotes.does: Saved and exported with your character. The rules never read these notes.

notesDetails.title: Notes Details
notesDetails.does: Reference only; nothing to choose here.
